draft.title: The Australian Consumer Law
card: The Australian Consumer Law (ACL) is a set of rules that protects buyers in every state and territory. It applies to businesses that sell goods and services to consumers.
Products must be safe to use in the ways they are meant to be used.
Products must do the job they are made for and last a reasonable time.
Products must be as they were described, such as in an advertisement, on the packaging or by a salesperson.
draft.remember: The ACL protects buyers everywhere in Australia: products must be safe, work properly and match their description.

a.q: Jai buys a torch labelled "waterproof". It stops working after one splash. Which part of the ACL does this break?
opts: The product does not match its description
The product is not sold in his state
The product is not safe to hold
The product is not made in Australia
a.why: The label said waterproof, but the torch failed in water, so it did not match its description. The ACL does not ask where a product is made, and nothing here suggests the torch was unsafe.
a.clue: Compare what the label promised with what happened.

b.q: Priya buys a hair dryer in Geelong. It overheats and gives her a burn when she uses it normally. Which guarantee has the seller failed to meet?
opts: The product must be safe to use
The product must match its description
The product must be sold at a fair price
The product must come with a free repair
b.why: A hair dryer that burns someone during normal use is not safe. It may also not work as it should, but the main failure is safety. The ACL does not set prices or promise free repairs.
b.clue: Think about what harmed Priya when she used it normally.

a.best: The product does not match its description

b.best: The product must be safe to use
